clue.text: In the style of the pilgrims' tales by the way

definitions.text: In the style of the pilgrims' tales by the way

parts.words: In the style of the pilgrims' tales by the way
parts.note: the Canterbury pilgrims told their stories to pass the time while travelling the road, so the clue describes writing like that fourteenth-century poet's

explanation.walkthrough: 'By the way' sounds like a throwaway aside, but it is literal: the tales were told on the way to Canterbury.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything resembling the work of the poet of the Canterbury Tales.

clue.text: Deal successfully with an outer garment

definitions.meaning: to manage or handle a problem well
a long cloak worn by a priest at certain services

explanation.surface: Someone manages to deal with an overcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage a difficulty is the verb sense; the noun is a priest's ceremonial cape.

clue.text: Stimulation caused by all first University orals

indicators.note: first picks out only the opening letter of the word all
the loose phrase says the answer is produced from the letters that follow, rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Excitement brought on by sitting all the spoken examinations at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caused by' signals the anagram of A (first of 'all'), U and ORALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stirred up or excited is a kind of stimulation.

clue.text: Man in charge of goal post is made to ring the bell!

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the person who does the ringing

indicators.note: the letters are fashioned into something new, so this phrase calls for an anagram of the words before it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The fellow responsible for a goalpost is forced to sound the bell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is made' signals the anagram of MAN, IC and GOALPOST. The definition is loose: the answer is the one made to ring bells.
explanation.definitionFit: A bellringer, someone who studies or practises the art of change ringing.

clue.text: Remembered to phone again

definitions.meaning: rang a person a second time (past tense in the answer)

explanation.surface: Someone remembered to make another telephone call.
explanation.definitionFit: Brought to mind is one sense; the other is literal, called back on the telephone.

clue.text: Meat dish as the cook prepared it

indicators.note: a cook preparing food mixes and reworks it, so the two words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A meat platter served just the way the chef made it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook prepared it' signals the anagram of AS THE. An ASHET is a Scottish and northern English word for a large serving plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A large oval platter for serving joints, a dialect word from the French assiette.

clue.text: Me 'n' you heard 21

indicators.note: heard tells us the phrase is spoken out loud and we write what it sounds like

parts.note: the casual phrase said quickly sounds like a word for a list of dishes

explanation.surface: A playful spelling of 'me and you' said aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference to 21 across, THE BILL OF FARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant's list of dishes is called a bill of fare.

clue.text: Wriggling toes in a Baltic country

indicators.note: wriggling things squirm into new positions, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wiggles their toes in a country on the Baltic.
explanation.definitionFit: The northernmost of the three states on the eastern Baltic shore.

clue.text: Put below the music to emphasise it

parts.note: below means under
a score is the written music of a piece

explanation.surface: Put something underneath the sheet music to make it stand out.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing a line under words stresses them, hence to stress or highlight.

clue.text: The preface might be OK in verse

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the word for verse

parts.note: a poem is a piece of verse
R is Roger, the radio signal for understood or OK

explanation.surface: An introduction that might be acceptable when written in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'OK' is R (Roger, radio for 'all right'), set in POEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A proem is an introduction or preamble to a book or speech.

clue.text: Custom in the type of school where they lived together

indicators.note: in places the word for custom inside the school word

parts.note: a coed is a mixed school for both sexes
a habit is a custom or practice

explanation.surface: Tradition at a mixed school where pupils lived side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: COED is a co-educational, mixed school.
explanation.definitionFit: Shared a home, as couples do without marrying.

clue.text: Exclamation heard by unwell sailor on first class ship when gets given fish soup!

annotationWithheld.why: Exclamation heard by unwell sailor on first class ship when gets given fish soup!: BOO heard as BOU + ILL + AB + AI + SS gives twelve letters; nothing in the clue as held supplies the final E
annotationWithheld.clue: Exclamation heard by unwell sailor on first class ship when gets given fish soup!

clue.text: Sort of carpet not usually provided for someone who hasn't a bean!

definitions.text: Sort of carpet not usually provided for someone who hasn't a bean!

parts.words: Sort of carpet not usually provided for someone who hasn't a bean!
parts.note: a red carpet is rolled out for important guests, not the penniless; yet a red climbing plant grown for its pods shares the name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hasn't a bean' means penniless, but the answer is itself a bean, a climbing variety with red flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing plant with red flowers grown for its long edible pods; also a joking name for a red strip of carpet.

clue.text: When I sit on them they cost me time somehow

definitions.note: a plural noun phrase: groups a member sits on

indicators.note: somehow says the letters come out in some other order

explanation.surface: A grumble that sitting on boards wastes one's time.
explanation.definitionFit: Members sit on these working groups, which notoriously eat up hours.

clue.text: One who is about to see that things are right is a spectator

definitions.text: One who is about to see that things are right
definitions.meaning: someone who looks on, or checks things over, read as ON (about) plus a person who looks

explanation.surface: A supervisor who checks things is just a bystander.
explanation.definitionFit: A bystander who watches without taking part.

clue.text: Cicala performing in lyric style

indicators.note: performing suggests putting the letters through their paces in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A singing cicada performs a lyrical song.
explanation.walkthrough: The cicala (cicada) is an insect famous for its song, which fits the lyric surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after the Greek poet Alcaeus, a metre used in lyric verse.

clue.text: Traveller visits a street a long distance off with some hesitation

parts.note: a way is a road or street, as in Broadway
far means a long distance away
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A traveller hesitantly visits a distant street.
explanation.definitionFit: A wayfarer is one who journeys, especially on foot.

clue.text: The doctor's animal was found in the city

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor, so the doctor's gives MO'S
a cow is a farm animal

explanation.surface: The doctor's pet turned up somewhere in town.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Russia is a city.

clue.text: He composed at Manse

indicators.note: composed means put together anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man wrote music in a minister's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' is the anagram signal and also fits the composer defined. A manse is a minister's house.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedřich Smetana was the nineteenth-century Czech composer of Má vlast.

clue.text: Horseman with an offhand manner

definitions.meaning: casual or dismissive, showing lack of proper concern

explanation.surface: A rider with a careless attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalryman or knight on one hand; casually dismissive on the other.

clue.text: Passivity I retain somehow

indicators.note: somehow indicates the letters are put in some other order

explanation.surface: Somehow I hold on to my laziness.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendency to stay inactive or not change, i.e. sluggishness.

clue.text: Might be 6 or what comes after the repast perhaps

definitions.meaning: a reference to 6 across, a list of dishes

definitions.text: what comes after the repast perhaps
definitions.meaning: after the fare (meal) comes the bill, read whimsically

explanation.surface: A list of dishes, or the reckoning after dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: An old phrase for a restaurant's list of dishes; jokingly also the reckoning after eating.

clue.text: Member has nothing to dance about

parts.note: a limb, such as an arm or leg, is a member of the body
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A club member has nothing to dance about.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a joyless member, but 'Member' is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The West Indian dance in which one bends backwards under a low bar.

clue.text: Places where one might get called to or from the bar!

definitions.text: Places where one might get called to or from the bar!

parts.words: Places where one might get called to or from the bar!
parts.note: barristers' societies in London admit lawyers to practise; pubs have a bar from which drinkers are summoned at closing

explanation.walkthrough: The Inns of Court in London call students to the bar as barristers; a pub also has a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the legal societies and pubs go by this name.

clue.text: The European maestro was made of a rubbery substance

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the, a European language's article

indicators.note: made into something else, so the word beside it is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A famous European conductor was made of rubber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The European' looks like a person, but it is the Spanish word for 'the'; the maestro is only anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A polymer with elastic, rubber-like properties.

clue.text: Determined to attack

definitions.meaning: to assault, as in a dog ... someone

explanation.surface: Someone resolved to launch an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolved is one sense; the other is the phrasal verb meaning assault.

clue.text: Change over feet

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for feet is read backwards

parts.note: paws are animals' feet

explanation.surface: Switch feet round.
explanation.definitionFit: To exchange one thing for another.

clue.text: Undergraduate's first ancestors which became mistresses

indicators.note: became says the letters turned into something else, a rearrangement
first takes only the opening letter of the student word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A student's forebears who turned into kept women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'became' signals the anagram of U (first of 'Undergraduate's') and ANCESTORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Kept women or high-class prostitutes, especially at royal courts.
